title: features.py re-solves identical inputs: 60 main-process solves repeat one the same process already ran (exact, 3 runs)
claim: In a green run of tests/features.py, 60 HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize calls made in the script's own process receive input that pickles byte-identically to a call that same process already solved. The pickle covers the optimizer's __dict__ and the call arguments. It also covers the identity of every function and class bound in every loaded heatpump_optimizer module and in the class dict, so a mock.patch or class swap between two calls makes them distinct. The 60 are exact across three runs on two machines (box B3 Linux: 113 total minus 53 worker-process repeats; orchestrator M1 macOS: 60 of 266 hashed with the atexit hook, and 148 total minus 88 worker repeats with the per-solve snapshot). The largest site is _r9egb9_transport, with 28 repeats from one call site (17-31 s CPU, provisional), followed by _lg_band (10, a helper called with identical arguments) and _r9f13_inline (8). On top of these, the coordinator's persistent process_worker child repeats at least 53 solves (88 when every worker's record survives), at about 72 s CPU. That count is a lower bound: a worker killed at shutdown before atexit lost its record under the original hook, and a worker restart resets its memory. Under the same key, tests/optimality.py has 0 repeats of 23 solves, and its patched re-solves are not counted. dst_checks.py has 0 of 116.

evidence.unit: main-process repeated identical solves (sites with a tests/ frame); worker-process repeats >=53 lower bound (88 in repeat_solves_rerun2.out); repeat_cpu 52-123 s provisional
evidence.machine: box B3 (4 vCPU linux) and orchestrator machine (Apple M1, 8 cores, macOS); outputs repeat_solves_b.out, repeat_solves_rerun_atexit.out, repeat_solves_rerun2.out
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: another D3 seat and verifier seats on the same machine; macOS re-runs at load1 80-226 with swap nearly full. Counts are contention-immune; every CPU/wall number is provisional
evidence.tolerance: exact (main-process count); worker count is a lower bound

instrumented_symbol: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize (wrapped at module exec by a sitecustomize meta-path loader)

perturbation.change: repeat_solves.py --perturb-double: the wrapper solves each hashable call twice, restoring the pre-call __dict__ in between; repeats must rise by the hashed-call count
perturbation.observed_value: tests/manual_plan.py repeats 7 -> 38 (= 7 + 31 hashed calls), reproduced on macOS (repeat_solves_perturb_rerun.out)

null_control.note: open_meteo.py (no solve) reads 0 repeats in both arms; optimality.py's 4 patched re-solves read 0 under the identity key, so a deliberate mutation-proof re-solve is not counted

metric_definition: Count of optimize() calls in the script's own process (a tests/ frame on the stack) whose pickled (self.__dict__, args, kwargs, identities of heatpump_optimizer module callables and class attrs) equals an earlier call's in that process
phenomenon_property: A gate script solves a given optimizer input at most once per process. A check that needs the same plan again reuses the result, and a re-solve exists only where something in the input or the code differs.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub $HOME/venv-ci/bin/python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s3/repeat_solves.py $(python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s3/enumerate_m5.py | cut -f1 | grep '\.py$') lists every repeating call site per script
proposed_fix_scope: tests/features.py: memoise the solve in the helpers that repeat it, keyed on their arguments: _lg_band, and the _r9egb9 and _r9f13 transports' probe and null arms, which share a scenario. Do not memoise deliberate re-solves, such as determinism checks or patched-code arms. repeat_solves.py should read 0 repeats at the named sites afterwards.
reproduction_steps: subtract the 'repeat Nx at ?' line (worker-process solves) from RESULT repeats: 60
read 'repeat 28x at features.py:71641:_r9egb9_transport' and 'repeat 10x at features.py:40889:_lg_band'
